html:
Askar Akayev was the first president of independent Kyrgyzstan, from 1990 to 2005. He was born in 1944 in a village in the Chuy valley and trained as a physicist in Leningrad.

Unlike the other Central Asian leaders, he was not a party boss. In his first years he let in a free press, opened the economy fast on Western advice, and made Kyrgyzstan the first former Soviet republic in the region to bring in its own currency. Western donors called it an island of democracy.

Over time his family took over businesses and elections were rigged. After disputed elections in 2005, protests in the south and in Bishkek, the Tulip Revolution, drove him to Moscow, where he stayed. His successor fell the same way in the revolution of 2010.
